docs.title: Sign Language Learning App
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for the DSL Learning project! This application is designed to help users learn the NGT (Nederlandse Gebarentaal / Dutch Sign Language) alphabet using real-time computer vision and deep learning.

docs.title: Application Overview
docs.text: The app uses MediaPipe to detect hand landmarks and passes them to PyTorch models for classification: 1. Static CNN Model: Predicts letters A-I, K-Y. 2. Dynamic LSTM Model: Predicts letters with movement (J, Z) by evaluating a sequence of 30 frames.

docs.title: Getting Started Locally
docs.text:
Please refer to the setup scripts located in the scripts/ directory of the repository to automatically install dependencies and start the app:

# On Windows (PowerShell)
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
.\scripts\setup-windows-pwsh.ps1

# On macOS/Linux
./scripts/setup-unix.sh

Then start the application: 

uv run ./main.py

docs.title: Deployment & Architecture
docs.text: This guide explains the architecture of the DSL Learning app and how it is deployed.

docs.title: Local Development Architecture
docs.text:
During local development (and currently in production), the app uses a tightly coupled architecture:

  1. FastAPI Backend (main.py):
  2. Handles the WebSocket connections (/ws) for real-time model inference.
  3. Provides REST APIs (/api/*) for fetching assets and managing sessions.

  4. Serves the compiled Next.js frontend as static files.

  5. Next.js Frontend (frontend/):

  6. Built as a Static HTML Export (output: 'export' in next.config.ts).
  7. The compiled files in frontend/out/ are mounted by FastAPI and served directly.

When you run main.py, it automatically checks for model weights, ensures the frontend is built, and starts the Uvicorn server on localhost:8000.

docs.title: Production Deployment
docs.text: For a highly scalable production environment, the application is containerized using Docker and continuously integrated via GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Docker Architecture
docs.text:
The project uses a multi-stage Docker build to keep image sizes small and builds incredibly fast: 1. Node.js Stage: Installs npm dependencies and builds the Next.js static export (frontend/out). 2. Python Stage: Uses the highly optimized ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim base image. It syncs the Python environment perfectly using uv sync --frozen --no-dev, copies the frontend export, and sets the entrypoint.

Note: The MediaPipe and PyTorch models are explicitly not baked into the Docker image. The container dynamically downloads them at runtime using the logic inside main.py (check_and_download_models). This ensures the core Docker image remains small and easy to pull.

docs.title: Continuous Integration (CI/CD)
docs.text:
The project leverages GitHub Actions for CI/CD. The workflows can be found in .github/workflows/:

  1. docs.yml: Automatically builds and deploys this MkDocs documentation to GitHub Pages whenever changes are merged to the main branch.
  2. ci.yml: The main CI/CD pipeline.
  3. On Pull Request: Runs tests and linters for the Next.js frontend (using Node.js) and the FastAPI backend (using uv).
  4. On Push to main: Runs the tests/linters, and if successful, builds the multi-stage Docker image and pushes it directly to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io).

docs.title: How to use the Docker Image
docs.text:
Since the image is automatically pushed to ghcr.io, anyone (or any deployment platform like Google Cloud Run or Render) can pull and run the application:

docker pull ghcr.io/gfgf96/dsl-learning:latest
docker run -p 8000:8000 ghcr.io/gfgf96/dsl-learning:latest
